pairs.question: Exire ex urbe iubet consul hostem. Num in exilium?
pairs.answer: Non iubeo, sed, si me consulis, suadeo.
pairs.derivation: Cicero reports Catiline's implicit question and answers it himself. The preceding 'Exire ex urbe iubet consul hostem.' is kept verbatim as setup so 'in exilium' has a referent. The speech tag 'Interrogas me,' is dropped as framing/narration of the asking; the elliptical reported question 'num in exilium' is normalized to capital and a '?' (its words unchanged and in source order). The answer is Cicero's contiguous reply 'non iubeo, sed, si me consulis, suadeo', normalized to an initial capital and terminal full stop; nothing cut from it (a new section, 'VI. Quid est enim...', follows).

pairs.question: M.Tulli, quid agis? Tune eum, quem esse hostem comperisti, quem ducem belli futurum vides, quem expectari imperatorem in castris hostium sentis, auctorem sceleris, principem coniurationis, evocatorem servorum et civium perditorum, exire patiere, ut abs te non emissus ex urbe, sed immissus in urbem esse videatur? Nonne hunc in vincla duci, non ad mortem rapi, non summo supplicio mactari imperabis? Quid tandem te impedit? mosne maiorum? At persaepe etiam privati in hac re publica perniciosos cives morte multarunt. An leges, quae de civium Romanorum supplicio rogatae sunt? At numquam in hac urbe, qui a re publica defecerunt, civium iura tenuerunt. An invidiam posteritatis times? Praeclaram vero populo Romano refers gratiam, qui te, hominem per te cognitum nulla commendatione maiorum tam mature ad summum imperium per omnis honorum gradus extulit, si propter invidiam aut alicuius periculi metum salutem civium tuorum neglegis. Sed, si quis est invidiae metus, non est vehementius severitatis ac fortitudinis invidia quam inertiae ac nequitiae pertimescenda. An, cum bello vastabitur Italia, vexabuntur urbes, tecta ardebunt tum te non existumas invidiae incendio conflagraturum?
pairs.answer: Ego si hoc optimum factu iudicarem, patres conscripti, Catilinam morte multari, unius usuram horae gladiatori isti ad vivendum non dedissem.
pairs.derivation: The personified patria addresses Cicero with one extended plea/demand (a whole speech that is a question, its core being 'Nonne hunc in vincla duci, non ad mortem rapi, non summo supplicio mactari imperabis?'). The full quoted speech from 'M.Tulli, quid agis?' to '...conflagraturum?' is given verbatim and contiguous as the question, with the inline section markers [28] and [29] stripped as scaffolding (the source has 'M.Tulli' without a space, kept as-is). Cicero explicitly answers it: the framing 'His ego sanctissimis rei publicae vocibus et eorum hominum, qui hoc idem sentiunt, mentibus pauca respondebo.' is dropped as meta-narration of the answering; the answer's start is advanced to the operative sentence that directly answers why he does not have Catiline killed. The window ends at the first full stop ('...non dedissem.'); the following 'Etenim si summi viri...' begins elaboration/justification.
